The most appropriate ground is the **Speech or Debate Clause** (U.S. Const. art. I, §6, cl. 1), which gives members of Congress absolute immunity from civil suits over floor speech, so the complaint fails whatever its allegations of falsity or negligence. The team note on the Eleventh Amendment is wrong and doesn't apply here: it bars suits against states and state agencies, not individual officials sued for defamation, and it doesn't reach federal officials at all. The negligence-versus-actual-malice gap (the *New York Times v. Sullivan* standard for public officials) is only a weaker, secondary ground.

CONFIDENCE: 85
